newsitem.title: INDIA: India, China agree to cooperate in broadcasting.
newsitem.headline: India, China agree to cooperate in broadcasting.

text.p: India and China have agreed to exchange television programmes and jointly explore new broadcasting technology, the government said on Friday.
Representatives of the two countries signed a memorandum of understanding on Thursday in the Indian capital providing for increased cooperation in television, it said.

The agreement was signed by the director general of India's state television station Doordarshan, K.S. Sharma, and China's vice minister in charge of radio, film and television, Yang Weiguang, it said.
The two sides agreed to exchange television programmes in the fields of news, economic development, culture, education, children, science, technology, entertainment and sports.

"The two countries have agreed to explore and develop advancements in broadcasting technology including the exchange of information, the provision of technical assistance and the licencing of technology," it said.
During the visit by the six-member Chinese team, officials from the two countries agreed to exchange television series.
China and India fought a brief border war in the Himalayas in 1962 and their territorial dispute remains unresolved.
